full_text_en:
Construction Bank of China, Hefei Xinzhan Development Zone Sub-branch v. Anhui New Changjiang Company — dispute over loan contract

[Ruling Summary]

For a contract established before the implementation of the Contract Law, if the contract is invalid under the laws then in effect but valid under the Contract Law, the Contract Law shall apply.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2002) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 97

Appellant (Original Defendant): Anhui New Changjiang Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 85, Changjiang East Road, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Legal Representative: Bao Xianbin, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Li Yan, lawyer of Beijing Yuanzheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Shijia, lawyer of Anhui Chengyi Law Firm.

Appellee (Original Plaintiff): China Construction Bank, Hefei Xinzhan Development Zone Sub-branch, domiciled at Building 1, Master Plaza, Xinzhan Development Zone, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Responsible Person: Wang Bao'an, President of the Sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Geng Jiansheng, lawyer of Anhui Chengyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wan Xiaobei, lawyer of Anhui Chengyi Law Firm.

The appellant Anhui New Changjiang Investment Co., Ltd. appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2001) Min Er Chu Zi No. 16 rendered by the Anhui High People's Court in the dispute over a loan contract with the appellee China Construction Bank, Hefei Xinzhan Development Zone Sub-branch. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of presiding judge Liu Guixiang, judge Jiang Wei, and acting judge Wang Tao, to conduct the trial, with clerk Zhang Ruihua recording. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The Anhui High People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On August 15, 1996, China Construction Bank, Hefei Xinzhan Development Zone Sub-branch (formerly China Construction Bank, Hefei Railway Specialized Sub-branch; hereinafter referred to as Xinzhan Sub-branch) transferred HKD 20 million, which it had borrowed from Bank of China, Anhui Branch (hereinafter referred to as Anhui BOC), into the account numbered 139460000109 of the Hefei Branch of Anhui International Trust and Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Hefei Trust Branch) established at Anhui BOC, and at the same time instructed: "Please transfer to Anhe International Trust account number 13212002." On the same day, Hefei Trust Branch, through Anhui Anhe International Trust and Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Anhe Guotou Company), used a foreign exchange special income voucher to transfer HKD 20 million from its own account (i.e., bank deposit – Anhui BOC, account number 131002001) into the account numbered 13212002 opened by Anhui New Changjiang Group Investment Co., Ltd. (formerly Hefei Changjiang Supermarket Development Co., Ltd.; hereinafter referred to as New Changjiang Company) at Anhe Guotou Company. Thereafter, New Changjiang Company converted the foreign exchange into RMB in two transactions in August and October 1996, with the total converted amount of RMB 21,439,500 deposited into its RMB account numbered 80121219 at Anhe Guotou Company. On October 6, 1997, New Changjiang Company issued a letter of commitment to Xinzhan Sub-branch, stating: "Your Sub-branch's HKD 20 million loan in August 1996 was like charcoal in the snow. We will endeavor to repay HKD 5 million before the end of November 1997, another HKD 5 million before the end of February 1998, and the remaining HKD 10 million before the end of May 1998." On September 15, 1999, New Changjiang Company and its legal representative Wei Chao issued a fund utilization confirmation to Xinzhan Sub-branch, stating: "Our company (formerly Hefei Changjiang Supermarket Development Co., Ltd.) received HKD 20 million transferred from your Sub-branch's account number 139430000135 at Anhui BOC on August 15, 1996, for the construction of the Changjiang wholesale market. Our company hereby confirms this debt and will repay HKD 20 million to Anhui BOC within three months after the allocation of funds from the rights issue of our holding company next year, with the corresponding interest and expenses to be implemented in accordance with the relevant regulations of the People's Bank of China." On October 18, 2000, New Changjiang Company again issued a repayment plan to Xinzhan Sub-branch, stating: "Our company has repeatedly negotiated with your Sub-branch regarding the HKD 20 million transaction of August 14, 1996, and has proposed solutions. Due to the current tight financial position of the company, our company formulates the following repayment plan and requirements: 1. This amount shall be repaid in six quarters, with each quarterly repayment of HKD 3.5 million, and the balance settled in the sixth quarter. 2. This amount shall be remitted to an account designated by China Construction Bank, with our company only responsible for repayment in RMB, and the HKD to be arranged by your Sub-branch. 3. Request that the interest on this amount be reduced or waived." On February 13, 2001, New Changjiang Company instructed another party to pay HKD 379,620 on its behalf to Xinzhan Sub-branch, stating that it was for repayment of the loan borrowed by Xinzhan Sub-branch from Bank of China; on April 12, 2001, New Changjiang Company repaid another HKD 1 million.

On July 1, 1998, New Changjiang Company applied to Xinzhan Sub-branch, stating: "...We borrowed RMB 6.31 million in working capital from your Sub-branch, which has now matured. Due to recent cash flow difficulties, we specially apply to convert the RMB 6.31 million into a medium- to long-term loan"; on June 18, 1998, Xinzhan Sub-branch submitted a written request to China Construction Bank, Hefei Branch, proposing a specific plan to agree to the loan conversion with a term of 2-3 years. On July 21 of the same year, China Construction Bank, Hefei Branch agreed to the loan conversion and, in accordance with credit authority provisions, signed a loan contract with New Changjiang Company, stipulating: New Changjiang Company borrowed RMB 6.31 million, with a term from July 23, 1998 to October 22, 1999, monthly interest rate of 6.5175‰, etc. At the same time, the parties also signed a mortgage contract for real property, but did not complete the mortgage registration procedures. On August 14, 1998, Xinzhan Sub-branch transferred RMB 6.31 million to the New Changjiang Company account designated in the contract (account number 70726146058). After the above loan matured, Xinzhan Sub-branch sent collection notices to New Changjiang Company on October 19, 1999 and August 17, 2000, and New Changjiang Company confirmed and signed for the overdue loan collection notices, and on August 25, 2000 repaid principal of RMB 310,000, on May 31, 2001 repaid principal of RMB 300,000, on June 21, 2001 repaid principal of RMB 100,000, and paid all interest due before June 2001.

The Anhui High People's Court further found: On August 21, 1996, New Changjiang Company transferred RMB 10 million to Hefei Xingda City Credit Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as Xingda Credit Cooperative); on the same day, Xinzhan Sub-branch issued a certificate to New Changjiang Company, stating: New Changjiang Company repaid our Sub-branch a loan of RMB 6.91 million, with an actual payment of RMB 10 million, and the remaining balance of RMB 3.09 million was temporarily held by our Sub-branch (interest to be calculated separately); on August 4, 2000, Xinzhan Sub-branch submitted a request report to the Business Department of China Construction Bank, Anhui Branch, stating: ... on August 21, 1996, Xinzhan Sub-branch instructed the company (i.e., New Changjiang Company) to transfer RMB 10 million to Xingda Credit Cooperative to repay the RMB 10 million borrowed by the Railway Sub-branch from that cooperative, and at the same time offset the RMB 10 million loan of New Changjiang Company at the Railway Sub-branch. During this period, New Changjiang Company had multiple business transactions with Xinzhan Sub-branch and issued several fund utilization confirmations and repayment plans to the Sub-branch, but did not claim that the above RMB 10 million should be used to offset these amounts.

On August 6, 1999, China Construction Bank, Hefei Railway Specialized Sub-branch changed its name to China Construction Bank, Hefei Xinzhan Development Zone Sub-branch. On September 18, 1998, Hefei Changjiang Supermarket Development Co., Ltd. changed its name to Anhui New Changjiang Group Investment Co., Ltd. On October 30, 1995, Anhui Anhe International Trust and Investment Corporation was ordered to be dissolved, but it was not until 1998 that the People's Bank of China approved the cessation of its business activities, with all its civil liabilities to be borne by the Hefei Branch of Anhui International Trust and Investment Corporation.

The Anhui High People's Court held upon trial: 1. Although there was no written HKD loan contract between Xinzhan Sub-branch and New Changjiang Company, the flow process by which Xinzhan Sub-branch paid HKD 20 million to New Changjiang Company was confirmed by a series of interrelated evidence, and New Changjiang Company acknowledged the debt of HKD 20 million to Xinzhan Sub-branch in the fund utilization confirmations and repayment plans issued to Xinzhan Sub-branch from 1997 to 2000, and further repaid HKD 1,379,620 in 2001. Therefore, the act of lending HKD 20 million between Xinzhan Sub-branch and New Changjiang Company objectively existed, and the mutual expression of intent was also truthful and consistent; the lending relationship between the parties was established. However, neither party had the subject qualification for HKD lending, and the HKD lending was not approved by the foreign exchange authority. Consequently, the HKD lending relationship was invalid. New Changjiang Company should immediately return the HKD 20 million obtained thereunder. Given that New Changjiang Company has already repaid HKD 1,379,620, the outstanding HKD amount is HKD 18,620,380. Xinzhan Sub-branch's claim for repayment of this debt was legally founded, and the court upheld it. Xinzhan Sub-branch's application after trial to change this claim both violated procedural rules and did not conform to the objective facts, and the court did not uphold it. Both parties were responsible for the invalidity of the HKD lending relationship. Therefore, New Changjiang Company shall pay interest on the outstanding HKD at the prevailing HKD loan interest rate for the corresponding period from August 15, 1996 to the effective date of the first instance judgment, and other losses shall be borne by Xinzhan Sub-branch itself. Accordingly, Xinzhan Sub-branch's claim for repayment of interest on the outstanding debt was partially well-founded, and the court upheld it. New Changjiang Company's argument that there was no written loan contract with Xinzhan Sub-branch, that the HKD 20 million received was not paid by Xinzhan Sub-branch, that it did not actually use HKD, and that it should not be liable to repay the HKD 20 million was contrary to facts and law, and the court did not uphold it. However, New Changjiang Company's view that the interest rate provisions in the HKD loan contract between Xinzhan Sub-branch and Anhui BOC were not binding on it and should not serve as the basis for judgment in this case was legally founded, and the court accepted it. 2. The RMB 6.31 million loan contract signed between China Construction Bank, Hefei Branch and New Changjiang Company was based on the premise that New Changjiang Company had an overdue RMB 6.31 million loan from Xinzhan Sub-branch and applied for an extension. After Xinzhan Sub-branch reported it to China Construction Bank, Hefei Branch for review and approval, the contract was signed in accordance with the credit authority provisions between the higher and lower level banks. Xinzhan Sub-branch disbursed the loan in accordance with the contract and was the actual performing party of the loan contract. After the loan matured, Xinzhan Sub-branch sent collection notices to New Changjiang Company on October 19, 1999 and August 17, 2000, which New Changjiang Company confirmed on the overdue loan collection notices, and also repaid part of the loan principal and interest. Therefore, the mutual expression of intent between New Changjiang Company and Xinzhan Sub-branch to lend RMB 6.31 million was truthful and consistent. Although there were certain procedural flaws in the loan disbursement process, the rights and obligations of the two parties were clear, and Xinzhan Sub-branch had the right to assert this claim against New Changjiang Company. The court also upheld this claim. New Changjiang Company's defense that Xinzhan Sub-branch was not the creditor because the loan contract was not signed by Xinzhan Sub-branch was inconsistent with the objective facts, and the court did not accept it. 3. The act of New Changjiang Company transferring RMB 10 million to Xingda Credit Cooperative on August 21, 1996, based on the evidence adduced, should be characterized as a repayment by New Changjiang Company on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-branch. However, the aforementioned evidence at the same time showed that the purpose of New Changjiang Company's repayment on behalf was to offset its own loan at Xinzhan Sub-branch. Given that there were long-term business transactions between New Changjiang Company and Xinzhan Sub-branch, the evidence adduced by New Changjiang Company in its counterclaim was insufficient to establish that the repayment on behalf had been made. Therefore, New Changjiang Company's counterclaim lacked factual and legal basis, and the court did not uphold it. The contract in this case was established before the implementation of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, but there were no provisions in the law at that time regarding issues such as the establishment of the contract, and relevant provisions of the Contract Law may apply. In accordance with Articles 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 36, 52, 58, 107, and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. New Changjiang Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, return HKD 18,620,380 to Xinzhan Sub-branch; 2. New Changjiang Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay interest on the outstanding HKD to Xinzhan Sub-branch (interest calculated from August 16, 1996 to the effective date of this judgment on the actual outstanding HKD amount at the People's Bank of China's corresponding HKD loan interest rate for each period); 3. New Changjiang Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay RMB 5.6 million to Xinzhan Sub-branch; 4. New Changjiang Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay interest on the outstanding RMB 5.6 million to Xinzhan Sub-branch (interest calculated at 0.21‰ per day from June 21, 2001 to the effective date of this judgment); 5. Xinzhan Sub-branch's other claims are rejected; 6. New Changjiang Company's counterclaim is rejected. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 226,266 is to be borne by Xinzhan Sub-branch in the amount of RMB 45,253.20 and by New Changjiang Company in the amount of RMB 181,012.80; the property preservation fee of RMB 126,781.12 and the counterclaim fee of RMB 60,010 are to be borne by New Changjiang Company.

New Changjiang Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Anhui High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: The first instance judgment's finding that New Changjiang Company used the HKD 20 million was inconsistent with the facts. On August 14, 1996, Xinzhan Sub-branch borrowed HKD 20 million from Anhui BOC and transferred it, through Hefei Trust Branch, into the account established by New Changjiang Company at Anhe Guotou Company. To convert the foreign exchange into RMB, New Changjiang Company transferred HKD 19 million and HKD 1 million respectively on August 19 and October 7 of that year into the account of Hefei Trust Branch opened at Anhui BOC. Anhui BOC converted the amounts into RMB 20,368,000 and RMB 1,071,500 respectively on August 19 and October 8 of that year and transferred them into New Changjiang Company's account at Anhe Guotou Company. On August 20 of that year, New Changjiang Company, as instructed by Xinzhan Sub-branch, paid RMB 10 million to Xingda Credit Cooperative to repay a RMB 10 million borrowing of Xinzhan Sub-branch. This fact demonstrated that New Changjiang Company only utilized RMB 11,439,500 of the RMB converted from the HKD 20 million. The fund utilization confirmations and repayment plans issued by New Changjiang Company were not a true expression of intent and could not be used as a basis for determining that New Changjiang Company used the HKD 20 million. Because no HKD 20 million loan contract was signed between New Changjiang Company and Xinzhan Sub-branch, no loan relationship was established. Even if New Changjiang Company occupied part of the funds, it should only be liable to repay that part, not the full HKD 20 million, and certainly not the corresponding interest. Therefore, the first instance judgment, rendered without clarifying all the facts, erroneously ordered New Changjiang Company to repay the HKD 20 million principal and interest; the RMB 10 million that New Changjiang Company repaid to Xingda Credit Cooperative on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-branch was part of the RMB converted from the above HKD 20 million. The first instance judgment's finding that this RMB 10 million was used to offset other old loans owed by New Changjiang Company to Xinzhan Sub-branch had no factual basis whatsoever; the RMB 6.31 million loan contract signed between New Changjiang Company and China Construction Bank, Hefei Branch in 1998 actually converted old loans owed by New Changjiang Company to Xinzhan Sub-branch from 1993 to 1996 into medium- to long-term loans. After the conversion, New Changjiang Company repaid RMB 710,000 in principal, leaving an outstanding principal of RMB 5.6 million. However, since the previous old loans all lacked written loan contracts and were irregular loans, the interest of RMB 3,890,090.59 that New Changjiang Company had already paid on these irregular loans should be deducted from the outstanding principal. The first instance judgment's order that New Changjiang Company repay the principal and interest of RMB 5.6 million was improper. New Changjiang Company requested that the judgment be set aside, that the case be retried on the basis of clarified facts, and that Xinzhan Sub-branch be ordered to bear the case acceptance fee and litigation preservation fee.

Xinzhan Sub-branch argued in its defense: Because Anhui BOC could not directly enter into a foreign exchange financing relationship with New Changjiang Company, Xinzhan Sub-branch, as directed by New Changjiang Company, remitted the HKD 20 million into the foreign exchange account number 139460000109 established by Hefei Trust Branch, which had foreign exchange business qualifications, at Anhui BOC, with a notation to transfer to New Changjiang Company's account number 13212002 at Hefei Trust Branch; thereafter, the HKD 20 million in this case was converted into RMB by New Changjiang Company through Hefei Trust Branch and was entirely occupied and used by New Changjiang Company. New Changjiang Company issued a letter of commitment, fund utilization confirmation, and repayment plan to Xinzhan Sub-branch on October 6, 1997, September 15, 1999, and October 18, 2000 respectively, acknowledging receipt of the HKD 20 million and promising to repay it. Therefore, the evidence that New Changjiang Company obtained and used the HKD 20 million was sufficient, and the first instance judgment ordering it to bear the liability for repayment of principal and interest was correct. New Changjiang Company's grounds of appeal were inconsistent with the facts. Starting from July 1993, New Changjiang Company borrowed a total of RMB 14.91 million from Xinzhan Sub-branch in four separate loans. After New Changjiang Company repaid RMB 10 million on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-branch from the RMB converted from the HKD loan proceeds in this case, Xinzhan Sub-branch refunded RMB 1.4 million to New Changjiang Company through the account of Jintong Real Estate Company, and the remaining amount was applied to offset RMB 8.6 million of the above RMB 14.91 million in old loans. New Changjiang Company still owed an old loan principal of RMB 6.31 million. This fact was confirmed by New Changjiang Company in its interest repayment plan submitted to Xinzhan Sub-branch on August 10, 1998. Thereafter, New Changjiang Company repaid RMB 710,000 in loan principal to Xinzhan Sub-branch, leaving an outstanding balance of RMB 5.6 million. New Changjiang Company had always settled and paid loan interest to Xinzhan Sub-branch, signed and received Xinzhan Sub-branch's loan collection notices, and even proposed repayment plans, which also demonstrated that New Changjiang Company acknowledged the debt of RMB 5.6 million to Xinzhan Sub-branch. In summary, Xinzhan Sub-branch requested that the appeal be dismissed and the first instance judgment be affirmed.

Facts Found by the Court

On August 14, 1996, Xinzhan Sub-Branch and Anhui Branch of Bank of China entered into an interbank lending contract, stipulating that Anhui Branch of Bank of China would lend HKD 20,000,000 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch. On the same day, Anhui Branch of Bank of China transferred HKD 20,000,000 into the account opened by Xinzhan Sub-Branch with Anhui Branch of Bank of China. On August 15 of the same year, Xinzhan Sub-Branch transferred the said sum into account No. 139460000109 opened by Hefei Trust Sub-Company with Anhui Branch of Bank of China. On the same day, Hefei Trust Sub-Company, pursuant to the instructions of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, transferred the HKD 20,000,000 into account No. 13212002 opened by New Yangtze River Company with Anhe Guo Trust Company. On August 15 and October 7 of the same year, Xinzhan Sub-Branch transferred HKD 19,000,000 and HKD 1,000,000 respectively into the account opened by Hefei Trust Sub-Company with Anhui Branch of Bank of China for foreign exchange settlement. Hefei Trust Sub-Company transferred the total RMB 21,439,500, formed after the foreign exchange settlement by Anhui Branch of Bank of China, in two installments on August 20 and October 8 of the same year into account No. 801212194 opened by New Yangtze River Company with Anhe Guo Trust Company. On August 20 of the same year, New Yangtze River Company transferred RMB 18,367,000 from its account No. 801212194 into its account No. 70726146058 opened with Xinzhan Sub-Branch. On August 21 of the same year, New Yangtze River Company, pursuant to the payment authorization letter of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, paid RMB 10,000,000 to Xingda Credit Cooperative to repay the RMB 10,000,000 interbank borrowing owed by Xinzhan Sub-Branch to Xingda Credit Cooperative. New Yangtze River Company acknowledged the above flow of the HKD 20,000,000 in the supplementary explanation to its appellate brief submitted to this Court in the second instance. On the same day that New Yangtze River Company paid RMB 10,000,000 to Xingda Credit Cooperative, Xinzhan Sub-Branch issued a certificate to New Yangtze River Company, stating: "New Yangtze River Company repaid our bank a loan of RMB 6,910,000, with an actual payment of RMB 10,000,000; the balance of RMB 3,090,000 is temporarily retained by our bank (interest to be calculated separately)." On October 6, 1997, New Yangtze River Company issued a repayment undertaking letter for HKD 20,000,000 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch; on September 15, 1999, New Yangtze River Company issued a confirmation letter for the borrowing of HKD 20,000,000 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch; on October 18, 2000, New Yangtze River Company issued a repayment plan letter for HKD 20,000,000 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch. The contents of the above undertaking letter, confirmation letter, and repayment plan letter found by this Court are consistent with those found in the first instance. On February 13 and April 12, 2001, New Yangtze River Company made total repayments of RMB 1,379,620 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch.

During the period from 1993 to 1996, Xinzhan Sub-Branch and New Yangtze River Company conducted multiple loan transactions, but because these were off-balance-sheet transactions, no written loan contracts were signed. The lending relationships mutually acknowledged by both parties include: on July 14, 1993, a loan of RMB 2,800,000 to New Yangtze River Company; on May 4, 1995, a loan of RMB 1,760,000; on April 11, 1996, a loan of RMB 8,000,000; in 1996, a loan of RMB 2,350,000; totaling RMB 14,910,000 in loans. On August 20, 1996, New Yangtze River Company repaid RMB 8,600,000 in loan principal. As of June 20, 1998, New Yangtze River Company still owed Xinzhan Sub-Branch RMB 6,310,000 in loans. On July 1, 1998, New Yangtze River Company submitted a loan application report to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, proposing to convert the outstanding old loan of RMB 6,310,000 owed to Xinzhan Sub-Branch into a medium- and long-term loan. On July 21 of the same year, the superior bank of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, China Construction Bank Hefei Branch, based on the application of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, entered into a loan contract with New Yangtze River Company, stipulating a loan amount of RMB 6,310,000, with a term from July 23, 1998 to October 22, 1999. On August 14 of the same year, Xinzhan Sub-Branch, pursuant to the above loan contract, handled the loan rollover procedures for the RMB 6,310,000 for New Yangtze River Company. On August 10, 1998, New Yangtze River Company issued an interest repayment plan to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, stating: "New Yangtze River Company's original loans at Xinzhan Sub-Branch totaled RMB 14,910,000; on August 20, 1996, RMB 8,600,000 was repaid; the outstanding balance is RMB 6,310,000; and the interest is RMB 2,584,236.14..." After the loan contract term expired, Xinzhan Sub-Branch issued overdue loan collection notices to New Yangtze River Company on October 19, 1999 and August 17, 2000, respectively, and New Yangtze River Company affixed its official seal to each collection notice. New Yangtze River Company repaid a total of RMB 710,000 in principal to Xinzhan Sub-Branch on August 25, 2000, May 31, 2001, and June 21, 2001, and repaid all interest accrued prior to June 2001, leaving an outstanding principal of RMB 5,600,000.

On August 10, 2001, Xinzhan Sub-Branch filed a lawsuit with the Anhui High People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering New Yangtze River Company to repay HKD 19,620,380 and corresponding interest, RMB 5,600,000 and corresponding interest, and to bear the litigation costs. New Yangtze River Company filed a counterclaim, requesting a judgment ordering Xinzhan Sub-Branch to repay the RMB 10,000,000 that New Yangtze River Company had paid on its behalf to Xingda Credit Cooperative, and to bear the counterclaim litigation costs.

During the second instance, Xinzhan Sub-Branch asserted that although New Yangtze River Company had repaid RMB 10,000,000 on its behalf to Xingda Credit Cooperative, RMB 8,600,000 of that amount was used on August 20, 1996 to set off the old loan owed by New Yangtze River Company to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, and the other RMB 1,400,000 was returned by Xinzhan Sub-Branch to New Yangtze River Company through Jintong Real Estate Company on September 26, 1996. To support this, Xinzhan Sub-Branch presented to this Court a payment voucher issued by Jintong Real Estate Company for the payment of RMB 1,400,000 to Yangtze River Company.

In 1997, Li Laping, the president of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, was investigated by the procuratorial authorities on suspicion of economic crimes.

Opinion of the Court

This Court is of the opinion that: After Xinzhan Sub-Branch borrowed HKD 20,000,000 from Anhui Branch of Bank of China on August 14, 1996, it transferred the sum through Hefei Trust Sub-Company into the account opened by New Yangtze River Company with Anhe Guo Trust Company. On August 19 and October 7 of the same year, New Yangtze River Company, through Hefei Trust Sub-Company at Anhui Branch of Bank of China, converted the foreign exchange, and the settlement proceeds totaling RMB 21,439,500 entered another account opened by New Yangtze River Company with Anhe Guo Trust Company on August 20 and October 8 of the same year, respectively. Although New Yangtze River Company denied the above flow of HKD 20,000,000 during the first instance, it acknowledged this flow in the "Several Supplementary Explanations on This Case" provided during the second instance. Accordingly, it should be found that New Yangtze River Company obtained the HKD 20,000,000 borrowed by Xinzhan Sub-Branch from Anhui Branch of Bank of China and the corresponding RMB settlement proceeds. New Yangtze River Company conducted the foreign exchange settlement on its own after the HKD 20,000,000 entered its account; what Xinzhan Sub-Branch paid to New Yangtze River Company was HKD 20,000,000, not RMB 21,439,500. Therefore, New Yangtze River Company's appellate claim that even if it bore repayment liability, it should only be liable to repay in RMB rather than in HKD cannot be sustained. New Yangtze River Company issued a repayment undertaking letter, a confirmation letter, and a repayment plan letter to Xinzhan Sub-Branch on October 6, 1997, September 15, 1999, and October 18, 2000, respectively, confirming the fact of borrowing HKD 20,000,000 from Railway Sub-Branch. New Yangtze River Company argued that the repayment undertaking letter and other documents were issued at the request of Xinzhan Sub-Branch under circumstances where Li Laping, the president of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, was under investigation by the procuratorial authorities, and that these documents did not reflect its true intention. However, Li Laping was investigated in 1997; New Yangtze River Company still issued documents to Xinzhan Sub-Branch in 1999 and 2000 undertaking to repay the HKD 20,000,000 loan. Its argument that the repayment undertaking letter and other documents did not reflect its true intention clearly cannot be sustained. In the absence of New Yangtze River Company providing other contrary evidence or rebuttal evidence, this Court does not accept its claim; the repayment undertaking letter and other documents should serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case. Although Xinzhan Sub-Branch and New Yangtze River Company did not sign a HKD loan contract, the first instance's finding that the parties had actually formed a loan relationship for HKD 20,000,000, based on the fact that the HKD 20,000,000 borrowed by Xinzhan Sub-Branch from Anhui Branch of Bank of China entered New Yangtze River Company's account and the repayment undertaking letter and other documents issued by New Yangtze River Company, was not erroneous and should be affirmed.

After New Yangtze River Company converted the HKD 20,000,000 into RMB 21,439,500, it paid RMB 10,000,000 to Xingda Credit Cooperative on August 20, 1996, pursuant to the authorization of Xinzhan Sub-Branch. Whether this RMB 10,000,000 should be deducted from New Yangtze River Company's HKD 20,000,000 loan is the focus of dispute in this case. Xinzhan Sub-Branch contends that of the RMB 10,000,000 that New Yangtze River Company repaid on its behalf to Xingda Credit Cooperative, RMB 8,600,000 was used to set off part of the old loan owed by New Yangtze River Company to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, and RMB 1,400,000 was returned by Xinzhan Sub-Branch to New Yangtze River Company through Jintong Real Estate Company. Regarding the return of RMB 1,400,000, Xinzhan Sub-Branch provided the payment voucher of Jintong Real Estate Company and also provided an explanation issued by Jintong Real Estate Company during the second instance concerning its return of RMB 1,400,000 to New Yangtze River Company upon the authorization of Xinzhan Sub-Branch. New Yangtze River Company failed to provide corresponding rebuttal evidence, nor could it provide evidence that the RMB 1,400,000 was paid by Jintong Real Estate Company to New Yangtze River Company based on other reasons. Therefore, this Court accepts Xinzhan Sub-Branch's claim that it returned RMB 1,400,000 to New Yangtze River Company through Jintong Real Estate Company. Both parties acknowledge that as of August 1996, New Yangtze River Company owed Xinzhan Sub-Branch an aggregate of RMB 14,910,000 in old loans incurred between 1993 and 1996, and New Yangtze River Company repaid RMB 8,600,000 on August 20, 1996. New Yangtze River Company denies Xinzhan Sub-Branch's claim that this RMB 8,600,000 was set off using the above RMB 10,000,000, and argues that it was paid separately and unrelated to the RMB 10,000,000 it repaid on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-Branch to Xingda Credit Cooperative. However, because New Yangtze River Company cannot explain the manner in which it was repaid, nor can it provide the corresponding payment voucher for the separate repayment of the RMB 8,600,000; and because after it repaid the RMB 10,000,000 to Xingda Credit Cooperative on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, it issued undertaking letters and other documents to Xinzhan Sub-Branch three times, each time confirming that it owed Xinzhan Sub-Branch HKD 20,000,000 and proposing specific plans for full repayment, never once mentioning the offset of the HKD 20,000,000 loan by the RMB 10,000,000 it paid on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-Branch to Xingda Credit Cooperative, this Court does not accept New Yangtze River Company's above claim. Taking a comprehensive view of the facts, including that after New Yangtze River Company repaid RMB 10,000,000 to Xingda Credit Cooperative on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, Xinzhan Sub-Branch authorized Jintong Real Estate Company to return RMB 1,400,000; New Yangtze River Company acknowledged its debt of HKD 20,000,000 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch in writing three times; and New Yangtze River Company could not produce a payment voucher for a separate repayment of RMB 8,600,000 to satisfy its RMB loan obligation to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, it can be found that New Yangtze River Company used RMB 8,600,000 of the RMB 10,000,000 it repaid to Xingda Credit Cooperative on behalf of Xinzhan Sub-Branch to set off New Yangtze River Company's original RMB debt. Therefore, the RMB 10,000,000 that New Yangtze River Company repaid to Xingda Credit Cooperative on behalf of Railway Sub-Branch should not be deducted from the HKD 20,000,000 loan debt. New Yangtze River Company's appellate claim that it should only be liable to repay RMB 11,439,500 of the HKD 20,000,000 loan cannot be sustained, and this Court does not support it. The first instance found that the HKD loan contract was void because neither Xinzhan Sub-Branch nor New Yangtze River Company had the legal capacity to engage in HKD lending and the HKD loan in question had not been approved by the competent authorities; neither party raised any objection, and this Court affirms that finding. Although the HKD loan contract is void, New Yangtze River Company should not have used the HKD 20,000,000 without compensation. In addition to returning the outstanding HKD principal, it must also pay the corresponding statutory fruits, i.e., statutory interest. New Yangtze River Company's appellate reason and claim that it should not be liable to pay interest has no legal basis, and this Court does not support it. The HKD 20,000,000 was transferred into New Yangtze River Company's account on August 15, 1996. The first instance's judgment ordering New Yangtze River Company to repay the outstanding principal of HKD 18,620,380 owed to Xinzhan Sub-Branch and the corresponding interest from August 16, 1996 until the date this judgment takes effect was not erroneous and should be affirmed.

During the period from 1993 to 1996, New Yangtze River Company owed Xinzhan Sub-Branch a total of RMB 14,910,000. After the offset of RMB 8,600,000 on August 20, 1996, the outstanding balance was RMB 6,310,000. On July 21, 1998, to extend the repayment period of this outstanding debt and convert it into a medium- and long-term loan, the superior bank of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, China Construction Bank Hefei Branch, at the request of Xinzhan Sub-Branch, entered into a loan contract with New Yangtze River Company, stipulating a new repayment period from July 23, 1998 to October 22, 1999. Although this loan contract was signed by China Construction Bank Hefei Branch, the loan re-deposit voucher provided by Xinzhan Sub-Branch proves that the loan rollover procedures were handled by Xinzhan Sub-Branch, i.e., the loan contract was actually performed by Xinzhan Sub-Branch. Moreover, after the loan contract was signed, New Yangtze River Company's conduct—such as issuing an interest repayment plan to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, repaying RMB 710,000 in principal and all interest accrued before 2001 to Xinzhan Sub-Branch, and affixing its seal to Xinzhan Sub-Branch's debt collection notices—indicates that New Yangtze River Company acknowledged Xinzhan Sub-Branch as the counterparty to the RMB 6,310,000 loan contract. Therefore, New Yangtze River Company's appellate reason that Xinzhan Sub-Branch was not the creditor of the RMB 6,310,000 loan contract and had no right to assert claims against New Yangtze River Company is inconsistent with the facts, and this Court does not support it. The failure of Xinzhan Sub-Branch and New Yangtze River Company to enter into written loan contracts for the loans made between 1993 and 1996 violated Article 5 of the Loan Contract Regulations. However, pursuant to Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "when a people's court determines the validity of a contract, if a contract concluded before the implementation of the Contract Law would be invalid under the law in effect at that time but valid under the Contract Law, the Contract Law shall apply," the lending relationship between the parties during the period from 1993 to 1996 should be found valid. New Yangtze River Company's appellate reason that the loan contract was void, that it should not be liable to pay interest, and that the interest it has already paid should be set off against the outstanding principal cannot be sustained. The first instance's judgment finding the loan contract valid and ordering New Yangtze River Company to repay the RMB 5,600,000 in principal and overdue penalty interest was not erroneous and should be affirmed.

In conclusion, the facts found by the first instance are essentially clear, and the application of law is correct. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Judgment

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 226,266 shall be borne by Anhui New Yangtze River Group Investment Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
